correctness.rationale: For each generic pair of phase-coded Sturmian-integral words, reversal matching reduces exactly to the E_C reflected-cell overlap event on the length-m circle. Counting overlap of unit arcs yields the finite triangular sum (1); odd moduli give a constant length 1, even moduli 2 dist(C,2Z). The mismatch-count discrepancy is at most 2m times the standard arc discrepancy of an irrational rotation, uniformly over both phase choices. Every C is attained at every n by generic phase pairs, giving both Hausdorff inclusions and the minimum limit. Bounded partial quotients of alpha imply the same for alpha/m, hence O(log n). The standalone CHECK.py passes 1413 exact overlap identity tests, 252 independent finite-language comparisons and 28 brute minimum tests. No inference from finite enumeration to infinite quantifiers is used.

originality.rationale: The checked literature establishes strict ergodicity, interval coding, and exact reversal-count invariants for this setting or adjacent settings, but its statements do not imply asymptotic Hamming distance between arbitrary pairs of forward and reversed words. In particular, a known reflection-class theorem for the same modular-difference lift only detects exact reversal coincidence, whereas the new theorem obtains complete positive-density distance spectra and an odd/even phase transition. Semantic searches recovered no covering Hamming theorem; historical priority is necessarily provisional.

value.rationale: For a natural zero-entropy strictly ergodic family the result determines not merely whether reversal is exactly allowed, but how *all* forward words compare to reversals of all others at linear scale. For odd modulus every pair asymptotically has one prescribed distance, whereas even moduli realize every limiting distance in a nontrivial interval; the sharp minimum gap and O(log n) bounded-type error strengthen the classification. This is a structural parity boundary and complete natural invariant, beyond a textbook relabeling or isolated computation.
